question: What is the primary reason for keeping bed linen wrinkle-free?
explanation: Wrinkles in bed linen create friction and pressure points that can rapidly damage fragile skin and lead to pressure ulcers in immobile patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why should nurses avoid shaking soiled linen when stripping a hospital bed?

options.A: It prevents the dispersal of dust and micro-organisms into the air
options.B: It stops the linen from tearing into pieces
options.C: It saves time during the morning routine
options.D: It ensures the laundry bags do not get too heavy

explanation: Shaking linen aerosolizes dust, skin flakes, and pathogens, which can contaminate the surrounding environment and spread infection to other patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Where should soiled bed linen be placed immediately after removal?

options.A: Across the back of a wooden chair
options.B: Directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: On the floor near the patient's bedside
options.D: On top of the clean bedside locker

explanation: Putting dirty linen straight into a hamper prevents cross-contamination of furniture and keeps the environment clean. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: A nurse is stripping a contaminated bed. What action protects the uniform from pathogens?

options.A: Holding the bundle away from the face
options.B: Folding the linen into tiny squares
options.C: Washing hands before touching the sheets
options.D: Wearing a plastic apron during the procedure

explanation: A waterproof apron acts as a physical barrier preventing microorganisms from the linen from transferring to the nurse's uniform. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: How are the top covers typically arranged on an admission bed?

options.A: Spread flat across the entire mattress surface
options.B: Tucked tightly under the mattress at the top
options.C: Fan-folded to the side or foot of the bed
options.D: Rolled into a tight cylinder at the headboard

explanation: Fan-folding the top linen allows the new patient to slide into bed effortlessly without struggling with tucked-in covers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: The main purpose of preparing an admission bed is to...

options.A: Keep the room warm for patients with fever
options.B: Support a patient recovering from major surgery
options.C: Isolate an infectious patient from the general ward
options.D: Provide a welcoming and accessible setup for a new arrival

explanation: An admission bed is specially arranged so a newly admitted patient can settle in comfortably and quickly without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an operation bed?

options.A: To provide continuous traction for a fractured femur
options.B: To feed a patient who has difficulty swallowing
options.C: To receive a patient recovering from anesthesia safely
options.D: To isolate a patient with a severe airborne infection

explanation: Postoperative beds are specifically structured to ease patient transfer from theater trolleys and manage immediate recovery needs like vomiting or warmth. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why are hot water bottles sometimes placed in an operation bed before the patient arrives?

options.A: To sterilize the surface of the top cotton blanket
options.B: To dry out any moisture left on the mattress cover
options.C: To provide warmth for a patient prone to hypothermia post-surgery
options.D: To weigh down the bottom sheets against movement

explanation: Anesthetics can lower body temperature, so warming the bed helps prevent postoperative hypothermia, though care must be taken to prevent burns. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which patient condition is a cardiac bed primarily designed for?

options.A: Unconscious patients recovering from head trauma
options.B: Heart failure with severe breathing difficulty
options.C: Patients with severe burns over the lower limbs

explanation: Cardiac beds support patients who suffer from orthopnea and cannot breathe while lying flat on their backs. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does an overbed table help a patient in a cardiac bed?

options.A: It prevents them from trying to get out of bed unaided
options.B: It holds their food tray during regular feeding times
options.C: It lets them lean forward to use accessory breathing muscles
options.D: It supports their intravenous fluid infusion bags securely

explanation: Leaning forward onto a table reduces the work of breathing by engaging the shoulder girdle and accessory muscles of respiration. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the correct ergonomic action for a nurse before making a hospital bed?

options.A: Lower the bed to the lowest possible position
options.B: Adjust the bed height to waist level
options.C: Lock the wheels and step away from the frame
options.D: Remove the mattress to reduce heavy lifting

explanation: Raising the bed to waist height prevents the nurse from hunching over, protecting the lumbar spine from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why must bed wheels be locked during the bed-making procedure?

options.A: To reduce unwanted noise in the hospital ward
options.B: To make it easier to tuck the bottom sheets tightly
options.C: To prevent the bed from rolling away and causing a fall
options.D: To keep the mattress from shifting out of alignment

explanation: Unlocked beds can shift unexpectedly when a nurse leans against them, creating a major fall hazard for both staff and patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)
